record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
record.original_question: Consider the recurrence z_{n+1} = (alpha + beta z_n + gamma z_{n-1})/(A + B z_n + C z_{n-1}), for n = 0, 1, ..., and assume C > 0. If an equilibrium point of this recurrence is locally asymptotically stable, is that equilibrium point a global attractor for all positive solutions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order rational difference equation
  z_{n+1} = (α + β z_n + γ z_{n-1}) / (A + B z_n + C z_{n-1}),   n = 0, 1, 2, ...,
where the parameters α, β, γ, A, B, C are nonnegative real numbers with C > 0, and where initial conditions z_{-1}, z_0 are chosen so that the denominator A + B z_n + C z_{n-1} is positive for all n ≥ 0 (in particular, all positive initial conditions are admissible whenever the equation is well-defined).

An equilibrium of the equation is a point z̄ ≥ 0 satisfying
  z̄ = (α + (β+γ) z̄) / (A + (B+C) z̄).
Such an equilibrium z̄ is called locally asymptotically stable if it is Lyapunov stable and there exists δ > 0 such that every solution {z_n} with |z_{-1} − z̄| + |z_0 − z̄| < δ satisfies z_n → z̄ as n → ∞. The equilibrium z̄ is called a global attractor of all positive solutions if every solution {z_n} with z_{-1}, z_0 > 0 (for which the recurrence is well-defined for all n) satisfies z_n → z̄.

Question: Is it true that, for every choice of nonnegative parameters α, β, γ, A, B, C with C > 0, whenever an equilibrium of the recurrence is locally asymptotically stable, it is a global attractor of all positive solutions?
artifact.status_search_result: The question—whether local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity for second-order rational difference equations of this form—is a long-standing conjecture in the theory of rational difference equations (associated with Kulenović–Ladas and collaborators). Partial results are known for special parameter sub-cases, but a general proof or counterexample for the full family with C > 0 has not been reported in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: The global attractivity of some rational difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies partial cases of when local stability of an equilibrium implies global attractivity for rational recurrences.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results, not a full resolution, exist.

status_evidence.title: Global asymptotic stability in a rational recursive sequence
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses subcases of the general second-order rational recurrence and stability questions.
status_evidence.claim: General conjecture remains under active investigation in subcases.
